claims.text: Directional solidification can simultaneously enhance yield strength and tensile ductility in a brittle MPEA.
A conventionally cast HfMoTaTiZr or similar refractory MPEA has equiaxed grains, random grain-boundary orientations, and room-temperature brittleness.
A Bridgman process using a mold withdrawal speed of 3 mm/min through a water-cooled baffle is a demonstrated directional-solidification route.
Annealing at 900 °C for 50 h can optimize precipitate morphology and reduce the amount of a brittle Heusler-type phase.
Vacuum processing is required to prevent oxidation during the proposed route.
Directional solidification produces elongated grains aligned with the tensile loading direction.
Directional solidification avoids grain boundaries inclined at approximately 45° to the loading direction.
A reticulated microstructure promotes ductility by facilitating dislocation glide.
Fine spherical or sharp-cornered γ′ precipitates prevent formation of continuous brittle networks.
Removing 45° grain boundaries eliminates shear stresses on weak boundaries that would otherwise initiate cracks.
Annealing at 900 °C for 50 h reduces the Heusler-type phase fraction from about 9% to 3% and keeps γ′ precipitates smaller.
The proposed treatment maintains fine coherent precipitates that provide precipitation hardening without sacrificing ductility.
Solid-solution hardening can be retained while a reticulated Laves-containing structure improves ductility.
The proposed route will increase yield strength by a factor of 1.5–1.8 relative to conventional casting.
The proposed route will produce significantly higher tensile strain to failure than the brittle baseline.
Directional solidification will reduce the room-temperature standard deviation of ultimate tensile strength from approximately 50 MPa to below 20 MPa.
The hypothesis is limited to alloys whose primary failure mode is associated with transverse grain boundaries or brittle intermetallic networks.
Poorly controlled thermal histories can cause refractory MPEAs to form brittle secondary phases.
Hot isostatic pressing of TaNbHfZrTi can produce a secondary Zr/Hf-rich HCP phase and extremely poor tensile elongation.
Failure to significantly improve the product of yield strength and ductility is sufficient to falsify simultaneous improvement of both properties.

contradictions.description: Set B is explicitly assigned the 900 °C/50 h anneal while Set A is not, but the design subsequently states that both sets receive identical post-processing. This makes the treatment of the control ambiguous.

The hypothesis requires yield strength and ductility to increase simultaneously, whereas the principal falsification metric is their product. A large increase in one property could offset a decrease in the other and therefore fail to falsify the stated hypothesis.
